correctness.rationale: The unconditional triangle indicator has probability 1/4. For a pair at shorter separation δ∈[0,π] the conditional chance that an independently sampled third vertex makes a central triangle is δ/(2π); δ has uniform density 1/π. Integrating for δ≤α=πq gives joint probability q²/4 and Cov(H_ijk,J_ij)=−q(1−q)/4. An overlap of only one point gives zero by rotation invariance; disjoint supports are independent. Exactly 3*C(n,3) pair-in-triple incidences yield Cov(T_n,E_n,α)=−(n−2) C(n,2)q(1−q)/4. Edge indicators sharing a point remain uncorrelated; Var(E)=C(n,2)q(1−q). Distinct central-triangle indicators sharing two vertices have covariance Var(δ/(2π))=1/48, with C(n,2)(n−2)(n−3) ordered pairs; their Bernoulli variances give Var(T)=n²(n−1)(n−2)/96. Division gives Corr=−sqrt(3(n−2)q(1−q)/n). For n≥3 and 0<q<1 both variances are nonzero. q(1−q) has unique maximum at q=1/2. Endpoints q=0,1 correctly exclude Pearson correlation. Independent exact rational overlap/variance checks at n=3..18 and several q values corroborate the algebra, not the universal proof.
